name: Deramiocel (CAP-1002)
summary: Deramiocel (CAP-1002) is Capricor's allogeneic cardiosphere-derived cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, infused IV every 3 months, for any genotype. The Phase 3 is HOPE-3 (NCT05126758, n=106, age 10+, late- or non-ambulatory). It met its primary endpoint: PUL2.0 favoured deramiocel by 4.55% at 12 months, p=0.029 (Lancet 2026;408:721, PMID 42526472). The FDA advisory committee voted 3-9 against the cardiomyopathy indication on 29 July 2026. Capricor then amended the BLA toward an upper-limb indication, and the PDUFA date moved to 2026-11-22 (8-K 0001104659-26-100071). Price anchor: Duvyzat (givinostat), the genotype-agnostic DMD add-on, at a published $700,000 a year, less Sarepta's filed 21% DMD gross-to-net. Uptake anchor: more than 2,000 Duvyzat prescriptions in about two years, halved. Nippon Shinyaku is the exclusive US distributor. Capricor receives 30-50% of product revenue (10-K 0001104659-26-029580) but is in arbitration seeking rescission over a 'fundamental pricing flaw'. Second reader: the FDA disputes the efficacy claims (BioPharm International, 'FDA Disputes Capricor's Phase 3 Efficacy Claims'; STAT, 2026-08-20, reported the BLA 'heading for an FDA rejection'), and Capricor's two 2026 10-Qs no longer restate the 30-50% US share, which was last filed in the FY2025 10-K. Neither is a refusal: the BLA is pending, and the share is filed and in force until an arbitrator rules.

therapy_mode.source: HOPE-3, Lancet 2026;408(10556):721-733, doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(26)01385-1, PMID 42526472: 'Investigational product was infused intravenously every 3 months in outpatient settings'
therapy_mode.note: Repeated quarterly infusions with no fixed end, so chronic. The HOPE-2 open-label extension (NCT04428476) has dosed patients continuously since 2020
therapy_mode.check: PubMed PMID 42526472 (Lancet 2026;408(10556):721-733, doi 10.1016/S0140-6736(26)01385-1) abstract: 'Investigational product was infused intravenously every 3 months in outpatient settings'. Repeated dosing with no fixed end, so chronic is right. The HOPE-2 OLE continuing treatment is confirmed in the FY2024 10-K MD&A (book filing_sections, 0001558370-25-003707): '12 patients have elected to continue treatment of deramiocel'.

list_price_per_patient.source: Duvyzat (givinostat), ITF Therapeutics: 'The average annual cost of Duvyzat is $700,000 based on the typical patient studied in the clinical trial' (Managed Healthcare Executive, 'Nonsteroidal Drug for Duchenne Launches with a $700,000 Price Tag', managedhealthcareexecutive.com/view/nonsteroidal-drug-for-duchenne-launches-with-a-700-000-price-tag)
list_price_per_patient.note: JUDGEMENT on the comparator. The book has no CMS rows for any DMD drug (lookup.py demand returns nothing for Exondys, Vyondys, Amondys, Viltepso, Emflaza, Agamree, Duvyzat or Elevidys), so the anchor is a published annual list price. Duvyzat is the closest marketed comparator: a genotype-agnostic, chronic add-on to steroids, labelled for DMD from age 6 regardless of ambulation. Deramiocel would be the second such therapy. No deramiocel price has been disclosed. Case against: Duvyzat's $700,000 is weight-based for a typical EPIDYS patient (ambulatory boys), while deramiocel is a fixed quarterly dose, so the two need not price alike. The exon skippers (weekly IV, genotype-specific) and Elevidys (one-time) sit on different price bases. The NS dispute concerns the transfer price and Part B reimbursement, not the list price, but it may push the realised price down (see gross_to_net_pct)
list_price_per_patient.check: Search confirmed the Managed Healthcare Executive article: 'The average annual cost of Duvyzat is $700,000 based on the typical patient studied in the clinical trial', per an ITF spokesperson. FDA approval on 21 March 2024 for DMD age 6 and over, confirmed by the same search and the ITF launch release. lookup.py demand returns no rows for Duvyzat, givinostat, Exondys, Vyondys, Amondys, Viltepso, Emflaza, Agamree or Elevidys, so no CMS anchor exists and a published price is the right basis. Unit: 0.7 mm USD per patient-year = $700,000. The comparator choice is a labelled judgement with its case against: Duvyzat is oral and Part D, deramiocel is IV and Part B, and the dose is weight-based. Its inputs hold.

gross_to_net_pct.source: Sarepta FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-084144), note on reserves for discounts and allowances: 2025 provisions for chargebacks, rebates, prompt pay and other accruals of $503,131k against net product revenue of $1,864,296k (PMOs plus Elevidys). 503,131 / (1,864,296 + 503,131) = 0.2125 of gross
gross_to_net_pct.note: JUDGEMENT on applicability. The anchor is a published list price, so neither Medicare convention applies and a sourced discount is needed. Sarepta's DMD portfolio is the only filed DMD gross-to-net, and it carries the same Medicaid-heavy payer mix. Direction checked: 0.2125 comes off list, so net is $551,250 a patient-year. FY2024 was lower at 399,396 / (1,787,960 + 399,396) = 0.183. Case for higher: Capricor's complaint against NS says the agreement ties Part B reimbursement to Capricor's own sale price to NS, so providers would be paid less than they pay (Capricor release, 8-K 0001104659-26-057221; STAT, statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/05/08/capricor-accuses-nippon-slow-walking-plans-for-duchenne-drug; Fierce Pharma, fiercepharma.com/pharma/capricor-files-breach-contract-lawsuit-against-us-partner-ns-pharma). Until that is fixed, the realised price could sit well below list. Case for lower: Elevidys, a one-time gene therapy, is about half of Sarepta's gross, and its discount profile differs from a chronic infusion's
gross_to_net_pct.check: Read the Sarepta FY2025 10-K in the book (filing_sections, 0001193125-26-084144), reserves table: 2025 provision $503,131k (chargebacks 192,037, rebates 184,854, prompt pay 19,376, other 106,864), prior-year adjustments -$15,967k, total net product revenue $1,864,296k. 503,131 / (1,864,296 + 503,131) = 0.21252. Including the prior-year adjustment in gross gives 503,131 / 2,351,460 = 0.2140, the figure the DYNE-251 reader derived from the same table. The gap is immaterial. FY2024: 399,396 / (1,787,960 + 399,396) = 0.1826, as stated. Elevidys was 898,731 / 1,864,296 = 48.2% of 2025 net revenue, so 'about half' holds. Direction is right: share off list, net $551,250 = 0.7 x 0.7875. The anchor is a published price, so neither Medicare convention applies, and a filed discount is the right source. Caveat on the note: search confirmed the complaint says providers would be reimbursed less than their cost to acquire and administer the drug, across Medicare, Medicaid and private insurers (Capricor release 8-K 0001104659-26-057221 exhibit; STAT; Fierce). The specific mechanism, 'Part B reimbursement tied to Capricor's own sale price to NS', was not in anything I saw.

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of the treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: Grabich S et al., 'Real-world phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer treatment patterns in Duchenne muscular dystrophy: a claims-based analysis', J Comp Eff Res 2025;14(8):e250037, doi:10.57264/cer-2025-0037, PMID 40679364 (Inovalon claims, 397 US patients on the weekly-IV exon skippers): median time to a first gap of 60 days or more was 25.5 months, and 57.9% of patients with such a gap re-initiated
discontinuation_pct.note: JUDGEMENT on the derivation. The hazard of a 60-day gap, 1 - 0.5^(12/25.5) = 0.278 a year, times the 42.1% of gaps never restarted, gives 0.117 a year of permanent stops. The PMOs are the only chronic IV infusion in DMD with measured US persistence. Case for higher: deramiocel's patients are older (10+, mostly non-ambulatory), and their mortality is rising: median survival is 28.1 years for patients born after 1990 (Broomfield J et al., Neurology 2021;97:e2304, PMID 34645707). The study was Sarepta-sponsored, and re-initiation is counted within limited follow-up. Case for lower: quarterly outpatient dosing is less burdensome than weekly, and 12 of 13 HOPE-2 open-label patients were still being treated about 4.5 years in (FY2024 10-K 0001558370-25-003707; NCT04428476), which is 1.8% a year in a small, trial-selected group
discontinuation_pct.check: PubMed PMID 40679364 abstract (Grabich 2025, doi 10.57264/cer-2025-0037; Sarepta authors): Inovalon claims, 397 patients. Gaps of 60 days or more in 190 (47.9%), of whom 110 (57.9%) re-initiated. Median time to a first gap of 60 days or more was 25.5 months (IQR 22.3-32.9). Recomputed: 1 - 0.5^(12/25.5) = 0.2783; x (1 - 0.579) = 0.1172. Labelled judgement with a case each way. Broomfield (PMID 34645707) median 28.1 years for patients born after 1990: confirmed. The HOPE-2 figure: the FY2024 10-K says '12 patients have elected to continue treatment' in the OLE, and the book's trials table has NCT04428476 enrolment 13. The 10-K does not say all 12 were still treated 4.5 years in, so the 1.8% a year is looser than the note states. It sits only in the case for lower.

forecast_start_year.source: Capricor 8-K 0001104659-26-100071 (2026-08-24): PDUFA target action date extended to 2026-11-22 after a major amendment. HOPE-3 primary completion 2025-06-18 (NCT05126758, book trials table)
forecast_start_year.note: If the FDA approves on 22 November 2026, 2027 is the first full year. Case against, which could push it later: (1) the advisory committee voted 3-9 that the evidence did not support the cardiomyopathy indication (8-K 0001104659-26-088667), and the upper-limb indication is a late refinement; (2) a Form 483 followed the July 2026 BIMO inspection of HOPE-3 (8-K 0001104659-26-087891); (3) the NS arbitration is expected to begin in autumn 2026. Capricor says the agreement's pricing structure would 'impede patient access' to insured patients, so a launch under NS could slip until the dispute is resolved (10-Q 0001104659-26-097294). Mesoblast has also sued for patent infringement (July 2026, same 10-Q)
forecast_start_year.check: Filings read in the book (filing_sections). 8-K 0001104659-26-100071 (2026-08-24): PDUFA moved from 22 August to 22 November 2026, a major amendment with 24-month OLE data and 'a refined proposed indication focused on upper limb function'. 8-K 0001104659-26-088667: the CTGTAC voted 3 for, 9 against, 0 abstain on 29 July 2026 that the evidence did not support effectiveness for DMD cardiomyopathy. 8-K 0001104659-26-087891: BIMO inspection 6-20 July 2026 ended in a Form 483 with one observation (SOPs, documentation, vendor oversight, audit report timeliness in HOPE-3). The same 8-K revised the LVEF key secondary from p=0.04 to p=0.09. Q2 10-Q 0001104659-26-097294: arbitration expected 'this fall'; Mesoblast suit filed 16 July 2026. Book trials table: HOPE-3 primary completion 2025-06-18. Adds to the case against, from searches: STAT (2026-08-20) reported the BLA 'heading for an FDA rejection' and called HOPE-3 failed. BioPharm International ran 'FDA Disputes Capricor's Phase 3 Efficacy Claims'. The first BLA took a CRL in July 2025. 2027 stays: approval on 22 November 2026 makes it the first full year, and regulatory risk belongs in the engine's PoS. If a CRL issues, re-examine the asset for refusal.

exus_multiple.source: Capricor 10-Q 0001104659-26-097294: the European binding term sheet with Nippon Shinyaku expired on 1 April 2026 with no definitive agreement. In Japan, NS is exclusive distributor and Capricor 'is evaluating the regulatory pathway'. There is no ex-US regulatory filing
exus_multiple.note: Null, so the engine models the US only. No ex-US filing or commercial partner exists outside Japan, and the Japan share is an unquantified 'meaningful double-digit share of product revenue'. If an ex-US filing is made, the named comparator would be Sarepta's PMOs: rest-of-world $165,183k against US $800,382k in FY2025 (10-K 0001193125-26-084144), 0.2064, most of it early-access sales without EU approval
exus_multiple.check: Null holds. Q2 2026 10-Q MD&A (0001104659-26-097294, book filing_sections): the European binding term sheet 'expired in accordance with its terms on April 1, 2026' with no definitive agreement. Japan: NS is exclusive distributor for 'a meaningful double-digit share of product revenue'. Capricor has 'initiated regulatory engagement in Europe and Japan' to 'determine the most appropriate regulatory pathway'. There is no ex-US filing. The PMO split cited as a fallback is confirmed in Sarepta's FY2025 10-K: US $800,382k, rest of world $165,183k, 0.2064.

economics_share.unit: share of product revenue Capricor receives (lowest point of the filed range), not netted over a margin
economics_share.source: Capricor FY2025 10-K (0001104659-26-029580), MD&A, Collaborations, U.S. Distribution Agreement with Nippon Shinyaku (24 January 2022): 'Subject to regulatory approval, Capricor will have the right to receive a share of product revenue which falls between 30 and 50 percent.' Same wording in the FY2024 10-K (0001558370-25-003707). Capricor develops and manufactures; NS and NS Pharma distribute
economics_share.note: JUDGEMENT, and flagged for the company-rows step. By book convention the share is taken at the lowest point of the range, 30%. The book nets a received royalty as royalty / margin. This deal differs in two ways: Capricor bears manufacturing cost and NS bears selling cost, so the engine-ready value is (0.30 - cogs_pct - other costs Capricor keeps) / (1 - cogs_pct - sga_pct - rd_pct - other_costs_pct). Capricor has no company-level rows in the book, and no product revenue to draft them from, so the conversion cannot be done yet. 0.30 is the filed figure, un-netted. Not in this field: the $80mm approval milestone and up to $605mm in sales milestones. Case against: Capricor filed suit on 7 May 2026 seeking rescission, alleging a 'fundamental pricing flaw', and arbitration is expected to begin in autumn 2026 (10-Q 0001104659-26-097294). NS has counterclaimed. If rescission succeeds, Capricor sells directly and the share is 1.0 against its own selling costs
economics_share.check: FY2025 10-K MD&A (0001104659-26-029580, filed 2026-03-17, book filing_sections): 'Subject to regulatory approval, Capricor will have the right to receive a share of product revenue which falls between 30 and 50 percent.' Also confirmed there: $80.0mm approval milestone, sales milestones up to $605.0mm, Capricor responsible for development and manufacturing, NS and NS Pharma for distribution. The same sentence is in the FY2024 10-K. New finding: after the 7 May 2026 complaint, the Q1 (0001104659-26-060382) and Q2 (0001104659-26-097294) 10-Qs drop the US share sentence from MD&A and the notes, and still state Japan's. The 10-K remains the latest filed statement of the term. Dispute confirmed in the Q2 10-Q: the complaint alleges a 'fundamental pricing flaw' and seeks rescission; the injunction motion was withdrawn for arbitration 'this fall'; 'NS has asserted counterclaims'; Capricor 'continues to seek rescission'. DECISION, not a refusal. The share is sourced from a filing, and the agreement is in force until an arbitrator rules. The dispute brackets the outcome between two sourced cases: 0.30-0.50 of product revenue under NS, or 1.0 against Capricor's own selling costs if rescinded. Both give a revenue path, so RESEARCH_TASK's refusal test ('a partner whose share of economics cannot be sourced from a filing') is not met. Lowest point of the range follows the book's lowest-stated-tier practice (INCA33890, PF-08634404, disitamab vedotin seeds). On netting: forecast.py applies the share to rNPV, and the book has no CAPR company rows (no assets rows with assumptions, no data/assumptions CSV). The engine defaults cogs and sga to 0 (forecast.py: scalars.get('cogs_pct') or 0.0). Under those zeros, royalty / margin = 0.30 / 1.0 = 0.30, so the un-netted value is consistent with the book as it stands. It overstates Capricor by its manufacturing cost. When company rows land, it must be re-struck as the note says.

prevalence.source: Crisafulli S et al., 'Global epidemiology of Duchenne muscular dystrophy: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis', Orphanet J Rare Dis 2020;15:141, doi:10.1186/s13023-020-01430-8, PMID 32503598: pooled prevalence 7.1 per 100,000 males (95% CI 5.0-10.1). Applied to 168.34mm US males at 1 July 2024 (Census Bureau Vintage 2024 national estimates by sex, census.gov/data/datasets/time-series/demo/popest/2020s-national-detail.html; the total with 171.77mm females is 340.11mm). 168,340,000 x 7.1 / 100,000 = 11,952
prevalence.note: JUDGEMENT: a global pooled rate applied to the US population. lookup.py pool and epidemiology.csv carry no DMD figure, so this sets one. The note in the reply flags that DYNE-251 and SGT-003 in this batch share this indication and must carry the same number. Cross-checks: Capricor's own releases say about 15,000 US patients (8-K 0001104659-26-100071), and Solid Biosciences says 5,000 to 15,000 (8-K 0001193125-25-262795). The meta-analysis CI gives 8,417 to 17,002. The only US population survey, MD STARnet, reports Duchenne and Becker together, 1.38 per 10,000 males aged 5-24 in 2010 (Romitti PA et al., Pediatrics 2015;135:513, PMID 25687144), and gives no all-age count
prevalence.check: PubMed PMID 32503598 abstract: pooled prevalence 7.1 per 100,000 males (95% CI 5.0-10.1). 168,340,000 x 7.1e-5 = 11,952.1, and the CI gives 8,417-17,002. The pool is empty in the book: lookup.py pool Duchenne and epidemiology.csv return nothing. DYN_zeleciment_rostudirsen_dyne_251 already carries 11,952 / 367 from this seed. US TEST: MD STARnet (Romitti 2015, PMID 25687144, full text PMC4477633): in 2010 DBMD prevalence was 1.38 per 10,000 males aged 5-24, and DMD alone 1.02, stated as 1.12 in the Discussion; erratum PMID 25934896. The authors extrapolate DMD to all males at 0.3 per 10,000, 42% of Crisafulli's rate: 168.34mm x 3.0e-5 = 5,050 US patients. That extrapolation counts no one under 5 or over 24 and only definite or probable cases in 6 sites, so it is a floor, not an all-age estimate. MD STARnet boys aged 5-9 ran 1.93-2.05 DBMD per 10,000 (DMD about 71%, so about 1.4), against the birth prevalence's 1.98, which puts its ascertainment near 70%. A cohort check agrees with the pooled figure: 367 births a year x median survival 28.1 years (Broomfield, PMID 34645707) = about 10,300. No US all-age claims prevalence was found. PubMed and one web search surfaced only MarketScan cohorts (about 2,000 patients each) with no national rate. The German claims study (PMID 40804403) gives 14.85-18.91 per 100,000 males under 40. Other US figures: Capricor 'approximately 15,000' (8-K exhibits 0001104659-26-088667 and -100071, read); Solid 'an estimated prevalence of 5,000 to 15,000 cases in the United States' (8-K 0001193125-25-262795, read); Sarepta Q2 10-Q '1 in 3,500 to 5,000 males born'. Verdict: 11,952 sits inside the US bounds, 5,050 floor to 15,000 company figure. US surveillance leans lower, so the figure more likely overstates than understates. Labelled judgement, inputs confirmed, arithmetic exact.

incidence.source: Crisafulli S et al. 2020 (PMID 32503598): birth prevalence 19.8 per 100,000 live male births (95% CI 16.6-23.6). US births 2024: 3,628,934 (Births: Final Data for 2024, NVSR, doi:10.15620/cdc/252440, PMID 42378845). Male share at a sex ratio of 1,045 per 1,000 (Wikipedia, 'Demographics of the United States', 2022 figure; CDC's NVSR 53(20) trend analysis of the US sex ratio at birth puts it near 1,050) = 1,854,394 male births. x 19.8 / 100,000 = 367
incidence.note: Births affected per year, all of whom eventually reach the age-10 threshold. The engine passes incidence through eligible_pct (367 x 0.693 = 254 a year), which understates inflow to a 10-and-over pool that every surviving boy enters. The sex ratio's source is secondary, but a ratio anywhere from 1,040 to 1,055 moves the figure by less than 1
incidence.check: PubMed PMID 32503598: birth prevalence 19.8 per 100,000 live male births (95% CI 16.6-23.6). PMID 42378845 (NVSR Births: Final Data for 2024): 3,628,934 births. At 1,045 per 1,000: 3,628,934 x 1045/2045 = 1,854,394 male births; x 19.8e-5 = 367.2. Sex-ratio source is secondary but immaterial, as the note says. Sarepta's '1 in 3,500 to 5,000 males born' (20-28.6 per 100,000) puts 19.8 at the conservative end. The note on eligibility-filtered inflow (367 x 0.693 = 254) matches forecast.py, which multiplies incidence by eligible_pct.

eligible_pct.source: HOPE-3 entry criteria: male, 10 years or older, genetically confirmed DMD, PUL2.0 entry item 2-6 and total 40 or below, late-ambulatory (10 m walk/run over 10 s) or non-ambulatory, on stable corticosteroids; LVEF 35% or below and FVC under 30% of predicted excluded (Lancet 2026, PMID 42526472; NCT05126758 listing, clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05126758). Age filter derived from the pool itself: the stock under 10 is at most 10 years of incidence, 10 x 367 = 3,672, so the share aged 10 and over is at least 1 - 3,672 / 11,952 = 0.6928
eligible_pct.note: JUDGEMENT: only the age filter is applied. It is a floor for that filter, because counting every under-10 as diagnosed and alive overstates the young stock. Not applied, because no population share was found: the ambulatory-status and PUL2.0 entry-item filters, and the LVEF and FVC exclusions. Each would narrow the pool, so this overstates the trial population. The steroid requirement is also not applied, since FDA labels in DMD do not carry background therapy (Duvyzat's label is DMD age 6 and over). If the label did require steroids, MD STARnet's 68.9% initiation rate (Thomas S et al., J Child Neurol 2025, PMID 40879420) would give 0.477. Only 8.7% of MD STARnet adults were still on steroids at last visit (Jayaram MJP et al., Muscle Nerve 2026, PMID 42750368). The final label is open. Capricor asked the FDA to review a 'refined proposed indication focused on upper limb function' (8-K 0001104659-26-100071)
eligible_pct.check: PubMed PMID 42526472 abstract confirms HOPE-3 enrolled 'participants aged 10 years or older with DMD'. The age filter, the only one applied, holds. Recomputed: 10 x 367.17 = 3,671.7; 1 - 3,671.7 / 11,952.1 = 0.6928. Not re-verified, because the Amass quota was exhausted and ClinicalTrials.gov is blocked: the PUL2.0 entry, ambulation, LVEF and FVC criteria. They are listed in the note but not applied, so they do not move the value. MD STARnet steroid figures confirmed: PMID 40879420, 68.9% initiated; PMID 42750368, 67.1% ever used and 8.7% at last visit. Capricor's 'refined proposed indication focused on upper limb function' is confirmed in 8-K 0001104659-26-100071. Labelled judgement: it overstates the trial population, with the direction stated.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the eligible untreated pool started per year at peak
penetration_peak_pct.source: Duvyzat, the only genotype-agnostic DMD add-on launch: 'More than 2000 people with Duchenne have been prescribed DUVYZAT', including patients from the US and EU (duvyzat.com, ITF Therapeutics, as read in September 2026), against US approval on 21 March 2024 (8.86 mg/mL oral suspension, DMD 6 and over)
penetration_peak_pct.note: JUDGEMENT: 0.5x. Solved in the engine's identity: pool = US DMD aged 6+, 11,952 x (1 - 6 x 367 / 11,952) = 9,749, with inflow 299 a year, on the same Vyvgart curve (k 0.5633, midpoint 2.0). The peak that starts 2,000 patients over the first three model years (2024 partial to 2026) is 0.185. Deramiocel takes half: 0.0925. The halving covers the fact that the 2,000 is an upper bound for the US (it includes the EU and counts prescriptions, not starts). It also covers the fact that deramiocel is a quarterly infusion at a site of care, not an oral at home, with a modest effect (4.55% on PUL2.0) and a 3-9 advisory vote. Case for higher: late- and non-ambulatory patients have fewer options. Non-ambulatory patients were removed from Elevidys's indication in November 2025 (Sarepta 10-Q 0001193125-26-335003), and the exon skippers are genotype-specific. Duvyzat reached its pace while still ramping. Case for lower: the Part B reimbursement problem Capricor alleges in the NS agreement, and cell-therapy manufacturing capacity. Check: on these inputs the engine's treated stock reaches about 2,050 patients in 2032 and 3,700 by 2040, near 45% of the 10-and-over pool. For scale, Sarepta's PMOs have treated 'over 1,800 amenable patients worldwide' in a decade (8-K 0001193125-25-262591), against up to 29% of DMD being amenable (13% + 8% + 8%, Sarepta 10-K risk factors), about 3,470 US patients on this pool
penetration_peak_pct.check: Search confirmed duvyzat.com: 'more than 2000 people with Duchenne have been prescribed DUVYZAT, including global patients from the US and EU'. The page is undated, as read. US approval 21 March 2024, DMD age 6 and over. Solve reproduced with forecast.py's identity (derive_new_patients, s_curve): pool 11,952.1 - 6 x 367.17 = 9,749.1, inflow 367.17 x 0.8157 = 299.5, k 0.5633, midpoint 2.0. The peak giving 2,000 starts over indices 0-2 is 0.18496 (455 + 664 + 881), and half of that is 0.0925. Engine check reproduced: pool 8,280, inflow 254, discontinuation 0.1172. Treated stock is 2,056 in 2032 and 3,723 in 2040. Untreated stock in 2040 is 4,766, so treated plus untreated is 8,489 against a pool of 8,280. No carryover field is needed. Sarepta figures confirmed in the book: 'over 1,800 amenable patients worldwide' (8-K 0001193125-25-262591); 13% + 8% + 8% amenable (Q2 10-Q 0001193125-26-335003); 0.29 x 11,952 = 3,466. Removal of non-ambulatory patients from the Elevidys indication is confirmed in the same 10-Q. The 0.5x multiple is a labelled judgement with a case each way.

ramp_steepness.source: reused from the book's nipocalimab seed (lookup.py seed Nipocalimab): Vyvgart and Vyvgart Hytrulo Medicare beneficiaries across Parts B and D, 1,397 in 2022 to 4,310 in 2024 (lookup.py demand Vyvgart)
ramp_steepness.note: JUDGEMENT: the book has no DMD or neuromuscular launch curve (no DMD drug in drug_demand). Vyvgart is the book's measured launch of a rare-disease IV infusion billed mostly to Part B, the same care setting as a quarterly outpatient cell-therapy infusion. Duvyzat's two-year pace suggests DMD launches can ramp faster, which would move value earlier
ramp_steepness.check: lookup.py seed Nipocalimab: ramp_steepness 0.5633, Myasthenia Gravis, sourced to Vyvgart and Vyvgart Hytrulo Medicare uptake. lookup.py demand Vyvgart: Part B 879 + Part D 518 = 1,397 in 2022; Part B 1,653 + Part D 822 + Hytrulo D 86 = 2,561 in 2023; Part B 1,803 + Part D 947 + Hytrulo B 902 + Hytrulo D 658 = 4,310 in 2024.
